nodes.summary: For every infinite group $G$ there are subsets $A, B_1, B_2 \subseteq G$ such that $B_1$ and $B_2$ are both maximal under inclusion among the subsets $B$ for which the product $AB$ is direct, but $B_1$ and $B_2$ have different cardinalities. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 21.58 is negative.
nodes.title: No infinite group has equicardinal maximal direct factors

nodes.summary: The statement that there is an infinite group $G$ such that for every subset $A \subseteq G$, any two subsets $B_1, B_2 \subseteq G$ that are maximal under inclusion among the subsets $B$ for which the product $AB$ is direct have the same cardinality.
nodes.title: Infinite groups with equicardinal maximal direct factors (Kourovka 21.58)

nodes.summary: For subsets $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, the product $AB = \{ab \mid a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ is direct when each element of $AB$ is $ab$ for unique $a \in A$ and $b \in B$: whenever $a_1 b_1 = a_2 b_2$ with $a_1, a_2 \in A$ and $b_1, b_2 \in B$, we have $a_1 = a_2$ and $b_1 = b_2$.
nodes.title: Direct product of subsets
